page.layout: One printed page: running head at top; main text in a single wide column with verse lines set in indented italic; marginal notes in a narrow column at the right beside the text (letters a, b, c, d and references); catchword-like signature "Cc" centred below the text, followed by "isto-" at right.

main_text.p: pologia Origenisa, Ab his qui Origenis libros legunt, istud penitus putant exclufum esse mandatum, quo probabiles jubentur effici trapezitæ, scientes, quod bonum est retinere, ab omni autem specie mali se abstinere. Dubitari non potest, quin Eusebius, æque ac Clemens, & Basilius ad Paulum respiciat, cujus totam illam in priore ad Thessalonicenses ῥῆσιν recitat.T. 3. op. Bas. p. 36. col. 2. aut. med. Fronto quidem Ducæusb, nobilis Iesuita, ea de re non dubitavit, qui ad illum Basilii locum habet. Quæ sequuntur, ut bonus trapezita &c. alludunt ad illud Apostoli 1. Thessal. 5. 21. πάντα δοκιμάζοντες, &c. Eodemque refert illa Gregorii Nazianzenic, sane appositissimè;Iamb. 18.
main_text.l: Ἀγγυγογνώμων, εἴ τι μὴ καλὸν δέχυ·
Ἀπεπλέγυ δ᾽ἂν μή σε ποιεῖ βελτίω.
Siquid probandum est, accipe, ac per
main_text.p: Non dubitavit eruditissimus, atq; optimus Sylburgius noster, qui in notis ad locum Clementis nuper descriptum, Allusio (inquit d) est ad dictum Pauli 1. Thess. 5. Ex his nemo non videt, nihil esse necesse ad διαταγέας confugere, vel concedere eosp. 832. A.

page.notes: Marginal notes: "a Dissert. de Ignat. p. 85." beside the first paragraph; "b", "c" and "d" references as transcribed. Greek verse lines are reproduced as best read; the Greek of the first verse line and the Greek in "ῥῆσιν" and "διαταγέας" are uncertain and may contain errors. The "Cc" mark is a gathering signature. Marginal "Dissert." reference is partly illegible at the top right.
